intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Waikiki Beach Morning Family Swim
experiences.description: Start your day early at the iconic Waikiki Beach for a calm morning swim with the family. The gentle waves and lifeguard presence make it ideal for children. Rent bodyboards or try a beginner surf lesson as the sun rises. If midday heat or rain hits, head indoors to the nearby Waikiki Aquarium for an educational marine life experience.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Family Experience
experiences.description: Explore six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Enjoy cultural performances, hands-on activities like coconut husking and fire-making, and an evening luau show. This is a fully indoor and shaded experience, perfect for avoiding midday heat or rain. A top family-friendly cultural activity in Hawaii.

experiences.name: Lanikai Beach Early Morning Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle out to the twin Mokulua Islands from the pristine Lanikai Beach in the early morning when winds are calm and the water is crystal clear. Rent a two-person kayak suitable for older kids and adults. The calm turquoise waters and white sand make this one of Hawaii's most beautiful beach experiences. Return before midday heat peaks.

experiences.name: Bishop Museum Family Discovery
experiences.description: Visit Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum, perfect as an indoor alternative during midday heat or rain. Explore Hawaiian artifacts, a planetarium show, and interactive science exhibits that kids love. Learn about the history of the Hawaiian Islands, Polynesian navigation, and volcanic geology. Fully air-conditioned and family-friendly.

experiences.name: Sunset Luau at Paradise Cove
experiences.description: End your Hawaii trip with a memorable evening luau at Paradise Cove on the leeward coast. Enjoy traditional Hawaiian food including kalua pig, poi, and fresh seafood, along with fire knife dancing and hula performances at sunset. The event begins in the late afternoon and runs into the evening, perfectly avoiding midday heat. A magical family memory to close out the trip.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM via Alaska Airlines. Collect luggage, pick up any pre-booked rental car or take TheBus (Oahu's public transit, ~$3/ride) to your accommodation. Check in or store luggage if room isn't ready yet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Ala Moana Beach Park (free entry) — a calm, family-friendly beach perfect for a relaxed first afternoon. Let the kids splash in the protected waters while you soak in the Hawaiian sun. Grab shave ice from a nearby stand to cool off.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Ala Moana Center (open-air mall nearby) for window shopping and to get your bearings. Grab an affordable dinner at the Ala Moana Food Court featuring local plate lunch options.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport upon arrival — look for local options like a musubi (spam rice ball) for ~$2-3
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In near Kapahulu — famous local plate lunches for ~$10-12 per person
meals.dinner: Ala Moana Center Food Court — try L&L Hawaiian Barbecue for a classic plate lunch dinner under $12

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the midday arrival. Pick up a TheBus pass or grab a Biki bike share day pass ($15) for affordable local transport. Stop at a grocery store like Foodland to stock up on snacks and breakfast items to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Hawaii's most iconic snorkeling spots. Arrive early (opens 6:45 AM) to beat crowds and secure entry ($25/adult, kids under 13 free). Watch the free marine education video before snorkeling among colorful fish and coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Makapuu Point Lighthouse Trail (free) — a 2-mile round-trip paved hike with stunning ocean views. Families with kids will love spotting sea turtles and whales (seasonal) from the clifftop lookout.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kailua Town for a relaxed evening walk. Browse local boutiques and grab a casual dinner at a local eatery.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at the hotel using groceries purchased yesterday — cereal, fruit, and juice
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from your grocery haul to eat at Hanauma Bay picnic area
meals.dinner: Kailua Town — try Kalapawai Cafe & Deli for fresh sandwiches and local fare around $12-15

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online (book at least 2 days ahead). Bring reef-safe sunscreen (required by Hawaii law). Snorkel gear can be rented at the bay for ~$12. August weather averages 16.8°C highs — bring a light layer for the hike.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Diamond Head State Monument — Hawaii's most iconic volcanic crater hike. The 1.6-mile round-trip trail is manageable for families and rewards hikers with panoramic Honolulu views. Entry is $5/person or $10/car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Waikiki Beach (free) — the world-famous stretch of sand is perfect for swimming, building sandcastles, and people-watching. Rent a bodyboard (~$10/hour) for some family fun in the waves.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Kalakaua Avenue in Waikiki for the lively evening atmosphere. Watch free hula and live music performances often held at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free, nightly around 6:30 PM).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery — a Hawaii institution at ~$1.50 each
meals.lunch: Waikiki — try Marugame Udon for fresh udon noodles starting at $7, a budget-friendly and filling option
meals.dinner: Musubi Cafe Iyasume near Waikiki for affordable Hawaiian-Japanese fusion — meals under $10

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head opens at 6:00 AM — going early avoids heat and crowds. Bring water and sunscreen. The Kuhio Beach hula show is free and a wonderful cultural experience for the whole family. Parking in Waikiki can be expensive — use TheBus instead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center (PCC) in Laie on the North Shore. Purchase the basic admission package (~$60/adult, ~$48/child) which includes access to 6 Polynesian village exhibits. Spend the morning exploring Samoa, Fiji, Tonga, Hawaii, Tahiti, and Aotearoa villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring PCC — watch live cultural demonstrations including fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving. Kids will love the interactive activities. Enjoy the included canoe pageant on the lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the evening 'Ha: Breath of Life' luau show at PCC (included in some packages or add-on ~$20 extra). It's a spectacular family-friendly performance with fire dancing and Polynesian storytelling.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pack fruit and granola bars for the drive to the North Shore
meals.lunch: Gateway Restaurant inside PCC — all-you-can-eat buffet included in some packages or ~$25 separately
meals.dinner: PCC luau dinner buffet (if attending the show) or stop at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck on the way back (~$14 for a plate)

day_by_day.notes: PCC is about a 1-hour drive from Honolulu. Book tickets online in advance for discounts. This is one of the pricier days but offers exceptional cultural and entertainment value for families. Look for Costco or AAA discount packages to save up to 20%.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the North Shore to visit Waimea Bay Beach Park (free) — a stunning crescent beach with calm summer waters perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Walk up to the famous Waimea Bay rock jump (for older kids and adults).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along Kamehameha Highway stopping at Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach (Banzai Pipeline) — iconic surf spots that are calm and swimmable in summer. Explore the Haleiwa Town area with its charming surf shops and art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Haleiwa — browse the historic town and watch the sunset over the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from hotel groceries to eat on the road
meals.lunch: Haleiwa — Matsumoto Shave Ice is legendary (~$4-6) plus grab a plate lunch from a nearby food truck
meals.dinner: Haleiwa Joe's Haiku Gardens or Kono's Northshore for affordable burritos and local fare (~$12-15)

day_by_day.notes: North Shore beaches are significantly calmer in summer (August) than winter — ideal for family swimming. The drive along the North Shore is scenic and free. Bring a cooler with drinks and snacks to save money. August can have occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant site. The USS Arizona Memorial (free, but timed entry passes required — book online in advance) is a must-see. Arrive early as passes go quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center exhibits (free) and walk the grounds. If budget allows, add the USS Bowfin Submarine Museum (~$27/adult, ~$14/child) for an interactive family experience inside a real WWII submarine.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Honolulu and explore Chinatown — a vibrant neighborhood with street art, local markets, and affordable dining options.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pick up fresh pastries from a local bakery en route
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to eat at Pearl Harbor's picnic area — no outside food allowed inside the memorial but permitted in the parking/picnic zones
meals.dinner: Honolulu Chinatown — Little Village Noodle House for authentic Chinese-Hawaiian cuisine, meals ~$10-14

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is free but the boat ride to the USS Arizona Memorial requires advance timed-entry reservations at recreation.gov. No bags larger than a small purse are allowed — leave bags in the car. This is a solemn and educational experience appropriate for children 6 and older.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Manoa Falls Trail — a lush, jungle-like hike through a rainforest leading to a beautiful 150-foot waterfall. The 1.6-mile round trip is family-friendly and costs ~$5 parking. Wear water shoes as the trail can be muddy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lyon Arboretum (free or small donation) adjacent to the trailhead — 194 acres of tropical plants, orchids, and native Hawaiian species. Kids will love the exotic plants and peaceful setting.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kapiolani Park near Waikiki for a free evening picnic. The park often hosts free community events, concerts, and sports activities on weekends.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or smoothie bowls from a local cafe — look for deals around $8-10
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and fruit for a picnic at the arboretum
meals.dinner: Kapahulu Avenue — try Ono Hawaiian Foods for authentic local Hawaiian cuisine (laulau, poi, kalua pig) under $15

day_by_day.notes: The Manoa Falls trail can be slippery — wear closed-toe shoes with grip. The rainforest microclimate means this area gets more rain than the coast, so a light rain jacket is recommended. Mosquito repellent is a must for the trail.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kailua Beach — consistently rated one of Hawaii's best beaches. The powdery white sand and turquoise water are perfect for families. Rent kayaks (~$25/hour for a double) to paddle out to the Mokulua Islands offshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Lanikai neighborhood — a quiet, upscale residential area with a beautiful beach and the famous Lanikai Pillbox Hike (free, ~1 mile round trip) offering breathtaking views of the Mokulua Islands and coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Honolulu and visit the Aloha Tower Marketplace at the historic harbor for a relaxed evening stroll and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Kailua Town — Cinnamon's Restaurant for famous Hawaiian pancakes and local breakfast, ~$12-15
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua for fresh deli sandwiches and local snacks, ~$10-12
meals.dinner: Aloha Tower Marketplace — Gordon Biersch Brewery Restaurant for happy hour deals or nearby food trucks

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach has free parking but it fills up quickly — arrive before 9 AM. The Lanikai Pillbox hike is short but steep in places — manageable for kids 8 and older. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. The beach has no lifeguards so supervise children closely.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Exhibits cover Hawaiian royalty, natural history, and Pacific Island cultures. Admission is ~$25/adult, ~$17/child. The planetarium show is an extra highlight for kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Punchbowl Crater (National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific) — free to visit and offers panoramic views of Honolulu. A peaceful and historically significant site with beautiful grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Honolulu — return to Waikiki for a sunset beach walk and farewell dinner. Browse the International Market Place for last-minute affordable souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pick up fresh fruit and pastries from Chinatown's Oahu Market
meals.lunch: Bishop Museum Cafe or pack a lunch to eat on the museum grounds
meals.dinner: Waikiki — Duke's Waikiki for a splurge-worthy farewell dinner with ocean views (appetizers and happy hour deals available to keep costs reasonable, ~$20-25/person)

day_by_day.notes: The Bishop Museum is excellent for families with children — interactive exhibits and the Science Adventure Center are particularly engaging. Look for online discount codes or AAA discounts before purchasing tickets. The Punchbowl is free and a respectful, beautiful stop.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take a leisurely sunrise walk on Waikiki Beach or Ala Moana Beach Park. Collect any last shells, take final photos, and enjoy the peaceful early morning Hawaiian atmosphere before the beach crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation and head to the airport. Allow extra time for traffic and airport security. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts. Grab a final plate lunch at the airport's local food options.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii — carry the aloha spirit home! Review your trip highlights and start planning your next Hawaiian adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or grab a smoothie and acai bowl from a beachside vendor for a true Hawaiian farewell
meals.lunch: Honolulu International Airport — Makai Market Food Court for affordable local options including poke bowls and plate lunches
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11 AM — arrange late checkout if possible or store luggage at the hotel. Honolulu Airport (HNL) recommends arriving 3 hours before international/mainland flights. Use any remaining grocery items for a final picnic breakfast to minimize waste and save money.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.description: Start your day early at the iconic Waikiki Beach for a calm morning swim with the family. The gentle waves and lifeguard presence make it ideal for children. day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 11:20 AM — Flight Alaska lands. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation to the hotel. Check in early if possible or store luggage at the SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a short drive to nearby Knott's Berry Farm area or stroll Downtown Buena Park for a relaxed first afternoon. Visit a local grocery store to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first night — explore the Buena Park dining strip along Beach Blvd. Enjoy a low-key family dinner and rest up for the journey to Hawaii the next day.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bite at the airport before or after landing — airport café or sandwich shop
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or quick bite near the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Sizzler or Denny's on Beach Blvd, Buena Park — family-friendly, mid-range, approx $15–$25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Note: The hotel is located in Buena Park, California — not Hawaii. This appears to be the pre-departure accommodation. Days 1–2 are based at this location. Confirm onward flights to Hawaii and ensure all family travel documents are ready.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure near the hotel. Visit a nearby park or the Buena Park Mall for a relaxed family breakfast outing. Pack bags and prepare for departure to Hawaii.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to LAX or John Wayne Airport (SNA) for your flight to Honolulu, Oahu. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before departure. Enjoy airport amenities with the family.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Honolulu, Hawaii. Transfer to your Hawaii accommodation (hotel or vacation rental near Waikiki). Take a gentle evening stroll along Kalakaua Avenue to soak in the Aloha spirit for the first time.

meals.breakfast: IHOP or hotel continental breakfast near Buena Park hotel
meals.lunch: Airport terminal food court — budget $12–$18 per person
meals.dinner: Eggs 'n Things, Waikiki — iconic Hawaiian breakfast-all-day diner, great for families, approx $15–$22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your inter-island or mainland-to-Hawaii flight details. Waikiki is the recommended base for the Hawaii portion of this trip. Average August high is around 17°C (low-to-mid 60s°F) — pack a light layer for evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Waikiki Beach Morning Family Swim — Start your first full Hawaii day early at the iconic Waikiki Beach. The gentle, calm morning waves are perfect for families with children. Arrive by 7:30–8:00 AM before crowds build. Rent boogie boards from a beachside vendor ($10–$15/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Diamond Head State Monument (approx 10-min drive from Waikiki). Hike the 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit crater for panoramic views of Honolulu and the coastline. Suitable for families with kids aged 5+. Entry fee: $5/person.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a sunset stroll along the beachfront. Watch the famous Waikiki sunset from the beach or the Duke Kahanamoku statue area. Enjoy a relaxed family dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit, acai bowls, or malasadas from a local food truck near Waikiki Beach — approx $8–$12 per person
meals.lunch: Marukame Udon, Waikiki — famous for fresh udon noodles, very family-friendly, budget-friendly at $8–$14 per person
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — beachfront restaurant with Hawaiian-inspired menu, great ambiance, approx $25–$40 per person

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen — required by Hawaii law. Morning swim is best before 9 AM for calmer waters. Diamond Head hike takes approximately 1.5–2 hours round trip. Bring water and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Bishop Museum Family Discovery — Visit Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum in Honolulu. Explore the Hawaiian Hall, Science Adventure Center, and planetarium. Perfect for families and an excellent indoor option given August's occasional rain showers. Opens at 9 AM. Admission: approx $25 adults, $17 children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Iolani Palace (a short drive from the museum) — the only royal palace in the United States. Take a guided family tour to learn about Hawaii's monarchy history. Afterward, explore the nearby Chinatown district for a cultural walkabout.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the hotel pool or beachfront. Watch local hula performances often held free at the Kuhio Beach Hula Mound at sunset (check schedule).

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant, Kailua (or Waikiki location) — famous for Hawaiian-style pancakes and eggs, approx $14–$20 per person
meals.lunch: Café at Bishop Museum or nearby Helena's Hawaiian Food — authentic local plate lunches, approx $12–$18 per person
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood or Ono Hawaiian Foods — local favorite for poke bowls and Hawaiian plates, approx $15–$22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bishop Museum is highly recommended on rainy days. Book Iolani Palace tours in advance online. Free hula shows at Kuhio Beach typically run Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday evenings — verify current schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Lanikai Beach Early Morning Kayaking — Drive approximately 30 minutes from Waikiki to the stunning Lanikai Beach on the Windward Coast. Rent kayaks ($30–$50/hour for a double kayak) and paddle out to the twin Mokulua Islands. Morning winds are calm and ideal for families. Arrive by 7:00–7:30 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, relax on Lanikai Beach — consistently rated one of the world's most beautiful beaches. Build sandcastles, snorkel in the clear turquoise water, or simply unwind. Nearby Kailua Beach Park is also excellent for families with more amenities.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Honolulu via the scenic Pali Highway through the Ko'olau Mountains. Stop at the Nu'uanu Pali Lookout for dramatic valley views. Return to Waikiki for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Kalapawai Market, Kailua — beloved local deli with fresh pastries, sandwiches, and coffee, approx $10–$15 per person
meals.lunch: Buzz's Original Steakhouse, Kailua (casual lunch menu) or a beachside picnic from Kalapawai Market — approx $15–$25 per person
meals.dinner: Ramen Nakamura or Goma Tei Ramen, Waikiki — hearty, family-friendly, approx $14–$20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rentals available from Kailua Beach Adventures or similar local outfitters — book ahead in peak August season. Life jackets provided. Suitable for children 6+. Pali Lookout can be windy — bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Family Experience — Drive approximately 35 miles north of Waikiki to Laie on the North Shore. Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian villages (Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa). Participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire-making, and traditional weaving. Opens at 11:30 AM — arrive early for parking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center villages. Watch live cultural demonstrations and canoe pageants on the lagoon. The center is expansive — plan 4–5 hours minimum. Admission: approx $60–$80 adults, $48–$65 children (packages vary).
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the spectacular 'HA: Breath of Life' evening show at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a world-class Polynesian performance with fire dancing, music, and storytelling. Show typically starts at 7:30 PM. Dinner package available on-site.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab malasadas from Leonard's Bakery on the way out of Honolulu — a must-try Hawaiian treat, approx $8–$12
meals.lunch: Gateway Restaurant at the Polynesian Cultural Center — all-you-can-eat buffet with Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes, included in some packages or approx $25–$35 per person
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center (add-on package) — traditional imu-cooked kalua pig, poi, and Hawaiian sides, approx $35–$55 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets well in advance — very popular with families and often sells out in August. The evening show is highly recommended and worth the extra cost. Drive time from Waikiki is approximately 45–55 minutes. Consider carpooling or booking a shuttle.

day_by_day.morning: North Shore Beach Day — After yesterday's cultural immersion, enjoy a relaxed morning at one of Oahu's famous North Shore beaches. Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park for calm August waters (summer months bring gentle waves, unlike winter surf). Families can swim, snorkel, and explore the bay. The famous Waimea Bay rock jump is popular with older kids and teens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along Kamehameha Highway through the North Shore's charming Haleiwa Town. Browse local boutiques, art galleries, and surf shops. Visit Matsumoto Shave Ice — a legendary North Shore institution. Explore Haleiwa Ali'i Beach Park for more family beach time.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Honolulu via the scenic H-2 highway. Stop at Dole Plantation for a pineapple soft-serve and a walk through the world's largest maze (closes at 5:30 PM — time accordingly). Return to Waikiki for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Kono's Northshore, Haleiwa — famous for slow-roasted kalua pork breakfast burritos, approx $12–$16 per person
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck, Kahuku — iconic North Shore food truck, garlic shrimp plates, approx $14–$18 per person
meals.dinner: Teddy's Bigger Burgers or Lulu's Surf Club, Waikiki — casual, family-friendly, approx $15–$25 per person

day_by_day.notes: North Shore beaches in August have calmer summer swells — ideal for families. Always check ocean conditions before swimming. Matsumoto Shave Ice often has long lines on weekends — go early or be patient. Dole Plantation maze entry: approx $8 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Pearl Harbor Historic Sites — Take a solemn and educational morning visit to Pearl Harbor. Book the USS Arizona Memorial (free, but timed-entry passes required — reserve online weeks in advance). Also visit the USS Bowfin Submarine Museum and Park. A deeply meaningful experience for families with older children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Battleship Missouri Memorial (additional ticket: approx $29 adults, $15 children) — walk the decks of the famous 'Mighty Mo' where WWII surrender was signed. Afterward, head to Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (open Wednesdays, Saturdays, Sundays) for affordable Hawaiian souvenirs, local crafts, and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki. Enjoy a sunset beach walk and pick up any remaining souvenirs along Kalakaua Avenue. Treat the family to shave ice or fresh poke from a local market.

meals.breakfast: Boots & Kimo's Homestyle Kitchen (if in Kailua area) or hotel breakfast — approx $12–$18 per person
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor Visitor Center café or nearby Aiea restaurants — approx $12–$18 per person
meals.dinner: Yard House, Waikiki — large menu with something for everyone, family-friendly atmosphere, approx $20–$35 per person

day_by_day.notes: USS Arizona Memorial timed-entry passes are FREE but must be reserved online at recreation.gov well in advance — August is peak season and passes go quickly. Arrive 30 minutes before your timed entry. The experience is moving and educational — prepare children appropriately for the historical context.

day_by_day.morning: Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve Snorkeling — One of Hawaii's top family snorkeling spots. Arrive early (opens at 6:45 AM) as entry is limited and the bay fills up quickly. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel among hundreds of colorful tropical fish in the protected bay. Entry: $25 adults, free for children under 13. Closed Tuesdays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail (easy 2-mile round trip paved path) for stunning coastal views. Then visit Sea Life Park Hawaii nearby — a family-friendly marine park with dolphin encounters, sea turtle exhibits, and penguin shows. Admission: approx $40 adults, $25 children.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Waikiki — take a family sunset catamaran cruise from Waikiki Beach. Several operators offer 1.5-hour sunset sails with snacks and drinks (non-alcoholic options for kids). Approx $40–$60 per person. Book in advance.

meals.breakfast: Early morning — grab granola bars and fruit from a convenience store before Hanauma Bay (no food allowed inside the preserve)
meals.lunch: Kona Brewing Company, Hawaii Kai — fresh craft sodas for kids, great food, scenic harbor views, approx $18–$28 per person
meals.dinner: Arancino di Mare, Waikiki — upscale Italian with fresh Hawaiian seafood, a special family splurge night, approx $35–$55 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations are REQUIRED and must be booked online at hanauma-bay.hawaii.gov — book 2 days in advance (reservations open at 7 AM HST). Bring reef-safe sunscreen and snorkel gear (rentals available on-site). Sea Life Park dolphin encounters require advance booking and additional fees.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — early Waikiki Beach swim or sunrise walk along the beachfront promenade. Collect any last shells or photos. Visit the International Market Place for last-minute shopping — open-air mall with local vendors, Hawaiian jewelry, and gifts. Grab a final acai bowl or shave ice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sunset Luau at Paradise Cove — Head to the leeward (west) coast for the grand finale of your Hawaii trip. Paradise Cove Luau begins in the late afternoon (typically 5:00–5:30 PM check-in). Enjoy traditional Hawaiian games, crafts, and activities before the feast. Watch the imu ceremony (underground oven opening), then enjoy a lavish buffet of Hawaiian dishes.
day_by_day.evening: The Paradise Cove Luau culminates with a spectacular Polynesian show featuring hula dancing, fire knife dancing, and live music under the stars. A perfect, unforgettable finale for the whole family. Show ends approximately 9:00–9:30 PM. Return to hotel.

meals.breakfast: Heavenly Island Lifestyle, Waikiki — organic, health-focused breakfast with local ingredients, approx $14–$20 per person
meals.lunch: Light lunch — poke bowl from Foodland Farms or Aloha Poke Co., Waikiki — approx $12–$18 per person
meals.dinner: Paradise Cove Luau buffet dinner — included in luau package (approx $115–$145 adults, $75–$95 children depending on package tier)

day_by_day.notes: Book Paradise Cove Luau tickets well in advance at paradisecove.com — August is peak season. Transportation packages from Waikiki hotels are available and recommended ($20–$25 per person round trip). The luau runs approximately 4 hours total. Dress in aloha attire for the full experience. This is a wonderful way to end the Hawaii portion of the trip before returning to the mainland.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Waikiki Beach Morning Family Swim
experiences.description: Start your day early at the iconic Waikiki Beach for a calm morning swim with the family. The gentle waves and lifeguard presence make it ideal for children. Rent bodyboards or try a beginner surf lesson as the sun rises. If midday heat or rain hits, head indoors to the nearby Waikiki Aquarium for an educational marine life experience.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Family Experience
experiences.description: Explore six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Enjoy cultural performances, hands-on activities like coconut husking and fire-making, and an evening luau show. This is a fully indoor and shaded experience, perfect for avoiding midday heat or rain. A top family-friendly cultural activity in Hawaii.

experiences.name: Lanikai Beach Early Morning Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle out to the twin Mokulua Islands from the pristine Lanikai Beach in the early morning when winds are calm and the water is crystal clear. Rent a two-person kayak suitable for older kids and adults. The calm turquoise waters and white sand make this one of Hawaii's most beautiful beach experiences. Return before midday heat peaks.

experiences.name: Bishop Museum Family Discovery
experiences.description: Visit Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum, perfect as an indoor alternative during midday heat or rain. Explore Hawaiian artifacts, a planetarium show, and interactive science exhibits that kids love. Learn about the history of the Hawaiian Islands, Polynesian navigation, and volcanic geology. Fully air-conditioned and family-friendly.

experiences.name: Sunset Luau at Paradise Cove
experiences.description: End your Hawaii trip with a memorable evening luau at Paradise Cove on the leeward coast. Enjoy traditional Hawaiian food including kalua pig, poi, and fresh seafood, along with fire knife dancing and hula performances at sunset. The event begins in the late afternoon and runs into the evening, perfectly avoiding midday heat. A magical family memory to close out the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii — Flight Alaska lands at 11:20 AM. No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from the airport to your luxury hotel in a private chauffeured vehicle. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a leisurely stroll along Waikiki Beach to get your first taste of Hawaii. Dip your toes in the warm Pacific, explore the beachfront promenade, and let the family decompress from travel in a relaxed, scenic setting.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at a top Waikiki restaurant to celebrate the start of your Hawaiian adventure. Take in the sunset views over the ocean as you unwind.

meals.breakfast: Light snacks or meal on the flight before landing
meals.lunch: Azure Restaurant at the Royal Hawaiian — elegant oceanfront dining with fresh Hawaiian seafood and stunning Waikiki views
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — world-class Japanese-Peruvian fusion cuisine in a sophisticated setting, perfect for a luxurious first evening

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the late-morning arrival. Prioritize rest and acclimatization. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings and arrange private transportation for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Waikiki Beach Morning Family Swim — Head to the iconic Waikiki Beach early for a calm, gentle morning swim with the family. The protected waters are ideal for all ages, and the early hour means fewer crowds and cooler temperatures. Rent premium paddleboards or boogie boards for added fun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum for a Family Discovery experience — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Explore fascinating exhibits on Hawaiian history, volcanic geology, and Pacific Island cultures. An excellent indoor option that educates and entertains the whole family.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the upscale Ala Moana Center for some shopping, then head to dinner at a nearby fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Orchids at Halekulani Hotel — a legendary Waikiki breakfast spot with fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, and ocean views
meals.lunch: The Pineapple Room by Alan Wong — farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine inside Ala Moana, featuring locally sourced ingredients
meals.dinner: MW Restaurant — award-winning modern Hawaiian cuisine by chefs Michelle and Wade Ueoka, celebrating local flavors with a refined touch

day_by_day.notes: Book Bishop Museum tickets in advance online to skip queues. Waikiki Beach is walkable from most Waikiki hotels. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and water shoes for the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Lanikai Beach Early Morning Kayaking — Rise early and drive to the breathtaking Lanikai Beach on the Windward Coast. Paddle out to the twin Mokulua Islands in calm morning waters with a private guided kayak tour. The turquoise lagoon and white sand are among Hawaii's most stunning scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming town of Kailua nearby — browse boutique shops, visit the Kailua Beach Park, and enjoy the laid-back windward atmosphere. Optionally, book a private snorkeling excursion in the crystal-clear waters off Kailua.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Honolulu for a refined dinner experience in the heart of the city.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at your hotel before departure — grab fresh fruit, pastries, and coffee from the hotel's premium breakfast service
meals.lunch: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua — beloved local gem known for creative pancakes and hearty Hawaiian-style brunch plates
meals.dinner: Alan Wong's Honolulu — one of Hawaii's most celebrated fine dining institutions, showcasing the best of Hawaii Regional Cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach is approximately 30–40 minutes from Waikiki by private car. Book kayak rentals or guided tours in advance. Start early (by 7:00–7:30 AM) to enjoy the calmest winds and most beautiful light for kayaking.

day_by_day.morning: Private Diamond Head Crater Hike — Embark on a guided family hike up the iconic Diamond Head State Monument. The moderate trail rewards hikers with panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. A private guide enhances the experience with geological and cultural storytelling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and recharge at your hotel's luxury pool or private beach cabana. Enjoy spa treatments at the hotel spa — book massages or family-friendly treatments for a mid-trip refresh.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar followed by a premium dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: The Veranda at Moana Surfrider — a historic beachfront setting serving a lavish breakfast spread with fresh Hawaiian produce
meals.lunch: In-room or poolside dining at your hotel — indulge in a curated luxury poolside menu with fresh salads, seafood, and tropical drinks
meals.dinner: Senia — a critically acclaimed Honolulu restaurant offering inventive tasting menus with global influences and local Hawaiian ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head hike is best done in the morning before heat peaks. The trail is approximately 1.6 miles round trip and suitable for older children. Bring plenty of water and wear comfortable shoes. Book spa treatments 24–48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Family Experience — Drive to the North Shore for an immersive full-day experience at the Polynesian Cultural Center. Explore six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Participate in hands-on cultural activities, traditional crafts, and live demonstrations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — watch the spectacular canoe pageant on the lagoon, try traditional foods at the village marketplaces, and enjoy interactive performances throughout the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Cap the day with the Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a premium luau experience featuring an imu ceremony, traditional Hawaiian feast, and a world-class Polynesian revue show.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure — fuel up with a hearty meal before the drive to the North Shore
meals.lunch: Gateway Restaurant at the Polynesian Cultural Center — enjoy an all-you-can-eat buffet featuring Hawaiian and Polynesian-inspired dishes
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Feast at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a lavish traditional Hawaiian luau dinner included with the premium luau package

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is approximately 35 miles from Waikiki (about 1 hour by private car). Book the Ali'i Luau package well in advance as it sells out quickly. The full experience runs from mid-morning through the evening show, making it a perfect all-day family outing.

day_by_day.morning: North Shore Surf Experience — Visit the legendary North Shore beaches including Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach (Banzai Pipeline). In August, waves are calmer and ideal for beginner and intermediate surfing. Book a private surf lesson for the family with a certified local instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Haleiwa Town on the North Shore — browse art galleries, surf shops, and local boutiques. Stop at the famous Matsumoto Shave Ice for a classic Hawaiian treat, and visit the historic Haleiwa harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a relaxing evening and upscale dinner.

meals.breakfast: Kono's Northshore — a beloved North Shore breakfast spot known for kalua pork burritos and fresh tropical smoothies
meals.lunch: Haleiwa Joe's Seafood Grill — a scenic waterfront restaurant in Haleiwa serving fresh local seafood with beautiful harbor views
meals.dinner: La Mer at Halekulani — Honolulu's most prestigious fine dining restaurant, offering exquisite French-Hawaiian cuisine in an elegant oceanfront setting

day_by_day.notes: North Shore is approximately 1 hour from Waikiki. August surf conditions on the North Shore are generally mild and family-friendly. Arrange private transportation for the day. Matsumoto Shave Ice may have lines — visit early or late afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Private Catamaran Snorkeling Cruise — Board a luxury private catamaran for a morning snorkeling excursion along Oahu's coastline. Explore vibrant coral reefs, encounter tropical fish, sea turtles, and possibly dolphins. Premium snorkeling gear, snacks, and beverages are provided on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve — one of Hawaii's most spectacular snorkeling destinations. Explore the protected marine sanctuary with its incredible biodiversity. Book a premium guided snorkeling tour for an educational and immersive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Waikiki with dinner at a celebrated local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light continental breakfast on board the catamaran — fresh fruit, pastries, juices, and coffee served as you sail
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch on the catamaran or at Hanauma Bay — premium catered boxes with fresh sandwiches, salads, and tropical fruits
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia Waikiki — Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's stunning Waikiki outpost offering bold Asian-inspired cuisine with premium ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations and has limited daily entry — book online weeks ahead. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Use reef-safe sunscreen only, as the bay is a protected marine sanctuary. Private catamaran charters should be booked at least one week in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Pearl Harbor Historical Tour — Visit the USS Arizona Memorial, USS Missouri Battleship, and the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum for a deeply moving and educational family experience. Book a premium guided tour for priority access and expert historical narration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Aloha Tower Marketplace and Honolulu Harbor waterfront area. Browse local artisan shops, enjoy the harbor views, and take a leisurely walk through the historic downtown Honolulu district, including Iolani Palace — the only royal palace on U.S. soil.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-finale dinner at one of Honolulu's top restaurants, celebrating a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things — a Honolulu institution famous for its fluffy pancakes, fresh omelets, and tropical breakfast plates
meals.lunch: Nico's Pier 38 — a beloved Honolulu waterfront restaurant known for ultra-fresh fish caught daily, served in creative preparations
meals.dinner: Vintage Cave Honolulu — an extraordinary underground fine dining experience offering one of Hawaii's most exclusive tasting menus with world-class wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is extremely popular — book tickets and guided tours well in advance. The USS Arizona Memorial may have wait times; a premium tour package often includes priority boarding. Iolani Palace tours also require advance reservations. Allow a full morning for Pearl Harbor.

day_by_day.morning: Private Helicopter Tour of Oahu — Soar above the island on a luxury private helicopter tour for breathtaking aerial views of Diamond Head, the Ko'olau Mountains, Waimea Valley, the North Shore, and the stunning Windward Coast. An unforgettable premium experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and enjoy your final full afternoon in Hawaii. Return to Waikiki Beach for one last swim, collect seashells, build sandcastles, and soak in the beauty of the Pacific. Optionally, book a private beachside cabana for a luxurious final beach afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Luau at Paradise Cove — End your Hawaii trip with a spectacular evening luau on the leeward coast. Enjoy traditional Hawaiian ceremonies, fire knife dancing, hula performances, and a lavish feast. A magical and memorable finale for the family.

meals.breakfast: Halekulani Hotel's House Without a Key — a legendary open-air breakfast and brunch spot with live Hawaiian music, hula dancing, and stunning ocean views
meals.lunch: Duke's Waikiki — a classic Waikiki beachfront restaurant celebrating surf culture with fresh Hawaiian seafood, tropical cocktails, and a lively atmosphere
meals.dinner: Paradise Cove Luau Feast — a grand traditional Hawaiian luau dinner included with your premium luau package, featuring kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour well in advance and confirm weight requirements for all passengers. Paradise Cove Luau is located on the leeward coast, approximately 27 miles from Waikiki — arrange private round-trip transportation. The luau typically runs from 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in Waikiki — Enjoy a leisurely last morning in paradise. Take one final sunrise walk along Waikiki Beach, collect any last souvenirs from the International Market Place or luxury boutiques along Kalakaua Avenue, and savor a relaxed farewell breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your hotel and transfer to Daniel K. Inouye International Airport in a private chauffeured vehicle. Allow ample time for check-in and security. Browse the airport's local shops for last-minute Hawaiian gifts, macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and local chocolates.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Hawaii — carry the aloha spirit home with you. Mahalo for a wonderful trip!

meals.breakfast: Heavenly Island Lifestyle — a beloved Waikiki café known for its organic, locally sourced breakfast bowls, acai plates, and fresh-pressed juices — a perfect healthy farewell meal
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport — Island Vintage Coffee at the Honolulu Airport offers excellent Kona coffee, fresh poke bowls, and Hawaiian snacks for a satisfying pre-flight meal
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or upon arrival at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — arrange a late checkout if possible to maximize your final morning. Confirm your departure flight details and arrange airport transfer the night before. Pack any perishable Hawaiian food items (like fresh pineapple) in checked luggage per TSA guidelines. Mahalo and safe travels!
